action.rationale: Fresh 10D problem with full budget available (evals_left=2000) and no incumbent; evaluations are cheap and deterministic. Probing (~12% ≈ 240 evals) will reveal basin structure to choose between local vs. global methods. This follows the probe-first principle to avoid committing prematurely.

Probes indicate a smooth near-quadratic landscape (P3 r2_quad_full=0.9682, r2_quad_sep=0.9398) and L-BFGS-B already achieved large gains to 782.13 in 32 evals per start (P4). Deterministic, cheap evaluations and 0 coords near bounds favor gradient-based local refinement from the incumbent.

L-BFGS-B is exhausted (exhausted=true after 550 evals) with best y=149.15, and progress has stalled for 21 evals. Probes indicate a smooth, near‑quadratic single basin (r2_quad_full=0.9682; fdc_spearman=0.6499), so a derivative-free trust‑region (BOBYQA) from the incumbent should refine efficiently.

Local polishers are exhausted (bobyqa exhausted=true after 107 evals; lbfgsb also plateaued) and we’ve stalled for 128 evals at y=149.15. Probes suggest a smooth, nearly quadratic landscape (P3 r2_quad_full=0.968) but a broader search may find a slightly better basin, so we’ll race CMA-ES vs TuRBO to pick the stronger explorer.

Both local solvers converged to the same value (lbfgsb: 550 evals best=149.15; bobyqa: 107 evals best=149.15), and we have stalled for 378 evals with no improvement. Probes indicate a near-quadratic, single-basin landscape (P3 r2_quad_full=0.9682), and the active CMA-ES already collapsed to a tiny sigma (4.43e-06) after 125 evals without gains. Further spending is unlikely to beat 149.15, so we finish early to save budget.
